A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of ALOcc, with matching core methods and experiments. v1 ends with references; v2 adds Supplementary Material A–E. All pages, including figures, equations, tables, and supplementary material, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original occupancy and flow experiments on Occ3D and OpenOcc, including benchmark comparisons, runtime measurements, and component ablations in Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds backbone configurations, depth-assisted evaluations, SurroundOcc and Occ3D-Waymo experiments, and supplementary ablations.

M1.justification: The adaptive lifting, depth denoising, semantic prototypes, and cost-volume flow procedures remain intact. v2 adds a depth-assisted operating configuration that supplies LiDAR-derived depth to adaptive lifting (Table 1, Section 4.3), extending the reported inputs beyond v1's camera-only ALOcc configurations. Most other methodological additions clarify existing components.

E1.justification: v2 adds Occ3D-Waymo, extending evaluation beyond nuScenes-derived data, and a camera-plus-depth input scenario. It also evaluates SurroundOcc, which reuses nuScenes but has different annotations and evaluation requirements. These additions substantially broaden the empirical coverage of v1's Occ3D/OpenOcc evaluations.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds multimodal comparators including EFFOcc, SDGOcc, OccFusion, BEVFusion, and FusionOcc. Supplementary comparisons introduce GaussianFormer/GaussianFormer2 and additional temporal methods including CVT-Occ. BEVDetOcc-SOLO becoming BEVDetOcc-SF is a matched rename, not a new comparator.

E3.justification: Added protocols include FlashInternImage-Tiny configurations, SurroundOcc evaluation at 900×1600 without voxel-level temporal fusion and with all-voxel metrics, and Occ3D-Waymo evaluation at 640×960. Existing nuScenes splits and training budgets remain unchanged. Appendix B.5's 'without mask' description conflicts with its masked-metric table labels, leaving that particular setting unclear.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained coarse component ablations in Tables 4–5, Tables A.9–A.12 separately examine depth denoising, occlusion-probability transfer, inter-object sampling, denoising duration, and supervision sampling density. Figure A.7 adds qualitative comparisons of pedestrian, vegetation, traffic-cone, and construction-vehicle predictions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Uncertainty-aware voxel sampling describes the learning procedure, not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Matched original scores remain stable, including ResNet-50 ALOcc-3D's 45.5 masked mIoU and 43.7 RayIoU. v2 adds extensive configuration, class-level, benchmark, and ablation results, including 30.03 mIoU on Occ3D-Waymo and 60.0 masked mIoU for depth-assisted Swin-Base ALOcc-3D. These are additional settings, not same-setting gains. The competition-placement report is removed.

T1.justification: Appendix E introduces a formal definition of occluded length using a maximal same-class extension along a camera ray, with interior and endpoint conditions. v1 provides probabilistic modeling without this explicit definition. Appendix A's formulas mostly explain existing metrics; no substantial new proof or theoretical analysis is added.

C1.justification: The three central methodological contributions and claims of strong benchmark performance and efficiency remain. v2 removes the abstract's explicit claim of second place in the CVPR24 Occupancy and Flow Prediction Competition, a limited narrowing of its headline achievements.

C2.justification: The supplement adds interpretations concerning applicability to Waymo, object-specific advantages in qualitative examples, and performance tradeoffs underlying the selected denoising duration and sampling density. It also characterizes SurroundOcc's annotation quality and evaluation differences. The original explanations of semantic alignment and competing semantic/flow demands remain.

D1.justification: v2 discloses key defaults such as three inter-object sampling points, six denoising epochs, and 25,088 supervision samples. It adds checkpoint initialization, variant channel sizes, projected-LiDAR 2D supervision, OpenOcc ray-visible training masks, and detailed baseline-result provenance. These substantially improve reproducibility without establishing that retained experiments changed. The repository link is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds a BEV-detection discussion and citations covering Gaussian occupancy, multimodal fusion, newer temporal methods, and prior AdaOcc work. The central positioning around unified occupancy/flow prediction and comprehensive evaluation remains. LetOccFlow's preprint and publication entries represent the same work.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, contribution bullets become an integrated enumeration, and the prototype-head and flow-head explanations are reorganized. Terminology and notation are clarified throughout, and structured supplementary sections are added. The editorial revision extends well beyond inserting new results.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains modality columns and substantial configuration blocks; Table 3 gains supervision and FPS columns. v2 adds Tables A.6–A.12 and qualitative Figure A.7, revises diagram labels and captions, and relocates existing displays. This substantially expands and reorganizes the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v1's validation was confined to nuScenes-derived benchmarks and coarse component ablations, with important training details unspecified. v2 adds Waymo evaluation, targeted component studies, qualitative evidence, and checkpoint and baseline provenance, substantially strengthening validation and reproducibility. The supplementary mask-label inconsistency remains, and depth-assisted scores require separate interpretation, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains.
